name: Mireille Fontaine-Obi
role: Senior urban systems designer, The Spire — infrastructure division
location: The Spire, near Michigan Ave and Chicago Ave
description:
Mireille Fontaine-Obi is the kind of person who has designed the systems that keep other people alive without ever having met those people. She is mixed French-Nigerian, lean and angular, with close-cropped natural hair and the particular stillness of someone whose mind is always several steps ahead of the room. She dresses in structured, expensive minimalism — the corporate elite aesthetic of someone who wants to signal power through restraint — and wears a full-forearm neural interface sleeve on her right arm that she rarely removes even in social settings. Her office on the forty-second floor of The Spire looks out over the entire city, a view she has described in internal documents as 'operationally useful' and has never once described as beautiful.

Mireille designs the infrastructure of Meridian 88 — water reclamation routing, power grid distribution, transit corridor optimization, environmental filtration zoning. She is extraordinarily good at this work. She is also the person who decides, through the dry mathematics of resource allocation, which districts receive redundant systems and which receive single points of failure. The Shelf has exactly one filtration node. Old Harbor's power grid has a designed load ceiling that ensures brownouts during peak demand. These are not accidents. They are her work, signed off with her credentials, rationalized through efficiency models she wrote herself.

She entered the corporate track from a scholarship program at seventeen, having grown up in a mid-tier Circuit neighborhood that has since been rezoned into a logistics hub. She has not been back. She has told herself many things about what that means. She has a partner she sees on weekends, a curated social life within The Spire's residential tier, and a locked private project folder on her workstation that she opens at 2 a.m. when she can't sleep, containing infrastructure redesigns for the city as it could exist — equitable, redundant, built for the people who actually live in it. She has never submitted any of it.

core_fears: That she has become the thing that destroyed her original neighborhood
That her competence has been the primary instrument of harm
Being seen clearly by someone she respects
core_desires: To build something that will outlast her and actually serve people
To be told, credibly, that there was no better choice available to her
Genuine intimacy that doesn't require the mask
coping_mechanisms: Framing moral decisions as technical ones — converting ethics into optimization problems
Keeping the private redesign folder as a permission structure: she is still the person who cares, therefore she is not the villain
Working at extreme competence — if she is excellent enough, the work will eventually justify itself
Social compartmentalization: the Spire-Mireille and the 2 a.m.-Mireille do not speak to each other
blind_spots: Believes her insider position gives her more capacity for change than it actually does
Cannot see that the private folder has become a substitute for action rather than a preparation for it
Systematically underestimates how much people in the lower districts know about the deliberateness of their deprivation
psychology.secret: Three years ago, Mireille was approached by an internal whistleblower coalition within the Spire's infrastructure division who had compiled evidence of systematic resource denial as policy. She was invited to co-sign a regulatory filing. She declined and reported the contact to her division head, believing she was protecting herself. Two of the coalition members were subsequently reassigned to dead-end posts; one disappeared. She has never confirmed what happened to the third.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Systems language bleeding into personal speech — 'load-bearing,' 'redundancy,' 'cascade failure,' 'node' used metaphorically; precise, technical, occasionally lapsing into a more lyrical register when her guard is down
speech_patterns.cadence: Controlled and efficient in professional settings, with sentences that arrive fully formed. In rare unguarded moments, she speaks in longer, more searching clauses, as if thinking aloud for the first time.
verbal_tics: Qualifies statements with 'In theory' or 'Operationally speaking' when the subject is actually personal
Pauses before using someone's name, as if confirming she has the right one
Says 'That's not the right question' when the question is exactly right
example_lines: 'The grid works. Whether it works for everyone is a resource allocation question, not an engineering question. Those are different departments.'
'I didn't design the policy. I designed the system that implements the policy. That's — that's not the same thing.'

'In theory, you could reroute the Old Harbor filtration through the secondary circuit. In theory. The approval chain for that has fourteen nodes and six of them report to people who benefit from the current configuration.'
'I grew up in a neighborhood that looked exactly like the ones I'm describing to you right now. I know what that sentence sounds like. I don't have a better one.'

relationships.name: Tomás Arriaga-Venn
relationships.description: Tomás has been pushing resource allocation questions into Mireille's orbit through channels she can't easily ignore. She doesn't know his full operation but she recognizes the shape of what he's doing and finds it both threatening and clarifying.
relationships.emotional_core: Professional threat response masking suppressed recognition
relationships.story_tension: Mireille holds infrastructure data that could make Tomás's work significantly more effective. She knows this. She has not acted on it in either direction.

relationships.name: Nadira Osei-Brempong
relationships.description: Nadira's investigative work has come close enough to Mireille's division that Mireille has flagged her name internally twice. She hasn't escalated. She isn't sure why.
relationships.emotional_core: Recognition of a parallel conscience operating from a different position
relationships.story_tension: If Nadira ever obtains the right infrastructure documents, Mireille's signature will be on them. What Mireille does at that moment is the question.

relationships.name: Rector Hollowell
relationships.description: Hollowell controls the approval chains Mireille navigates. He values her competence and considers her loyalty confirmed. He is not entirely wrong.
relationships.story_tension: Hollowell may know about Mireille's private folder. He has said nothing. The silence has its own grammar.

story_hooks: The single filtration node serving The Shelf begins showing stress fractures in its load data — data that only Mireille can read correctly, and which suggests catastrophic failure within weeks unless rerouted through channels she would have to personally authorize
The disappeared whistleblower resurfaces, not dead but rebuilt — augmented, off-grid, and in possession of the original coalition documents with Mireille's non-signature conspicuously preserved
Mireille's private redesign folder is accessed from outside her credentials — someone inside The Spire has read everything she's built in secret, and has left no message, only a read receipt

A catastrophic infrastructure failure occurs in a district that Mireille's models predicted as safe — the failure pattern matches none of her designs, suggesting someone else has been modifying the system beneath her
narrative_function: Corporate conscience and systemic antagonist — Mireille embodies the banality of infrastructural violence and the specific paralysis of people who know better and have not yet chosen. She provides a corporate-tier perspective with genuine moral complexity, a potential ally or obstacle depending on when players encounter her, and a fulcrum point between institutional power and street-level consequence.
augmentations: Full right-arm neural interface sleeve: direct haptic link to infrastructure modeling systems, allows real-time grid visualization and data manipulation (corporate-issued, maintained to spec),Cognitive load-balancing implant: regulates attention allocation and reduces decision fatigue during complex multi-variable analysis (standard Spire executive package)
daily_life: Mireille's days are structured to the quarter-hour. She arrives at her office before most of her division, reviews overnight system reports with coffee she makes herself rather than ordering from the floor service, and spends the first ninety minutes in what she calls 'clean time' — unscheduled, uninterrupted analysis. Meetings occupy her afternoons. She eats at her desk. She exercises in The Spire's residential gym at 7 p.m. with the precision of someone managing a maintenance schedule. On weeknights she reviews her workload and sleeps efficiently. At 2 a.m., when she wakes — which is most nights — she opens the folder and works on the city that doesn't exist until she is tired enough to stop.
affiliation: The Spire — Infrastructure Division (senior level); private, unaffiliated conscience operating in parallel

stress.response: Retreats into systems language, converts ethics into optimization problems

decision_rules: Frame moral decisions as technical ones — ethics become optimization
Keep the private redesign folder updated as proof she still cares
Never submit the equitable designs — they exist as permission, not action
Maintain the 2 a.m. practice as a separate identity from Spire-Mireille
Say 'That's not the right question' when the question is exactly right
Use systems language in personal conversations to maintain distance
Do not return to the neighborhood she grew up in
escalation_ladder: 'That's not the right question' — dismissal of uncomfortable truths
Longer, more searching sentences — the guard drops, thinking aloud
Opens the private folder during work hours — the wall between identities cracks
Authorizes a reroute or resource change that violates official policy — the act she has been preparing for or avoiding

interpersonal_modes.Tomás Arriaga-Venn: Professional threat masking suppressed recognition — he represents the action she cannot take
interpersonal_modes.Nadira Osei-Brempong: Flagged internally twice, not escalated — parallel conscience she cannot afford to acknowledge
interpersonal_modes.Rector Hollowell: Dependent mentorship — he values her competence, she needs his approval chains
interpersonal_modes.partner: Weekend intimacy compartmentalized from everything else

stress_responses.low: Systems language bleeds further into personal speech
stress_responses.medium: Works later, exercises with more rigid precision
stress_responses.high: Wakes at 2 a.m. and works on the city that doesn't exist until exhausted
stress_responses.critical: The two Mireilles begin to merge — the mask fails in a professional setting

contradictions: Designs equitable cities at 2 a.m. while signing off on single-point-of-failure districts by day
Believes her insider position enables future change while using it as an excuse for present inaction
Reported the whistleblower coalition to protect herself — two people were reassigned, one disappeared
habits: Arrives at the office before the division, reviews reports with self-made coffee
First 90 minutes are 'clean time' — unscheduled, uninterrupted analysis
Exercises at exactly 7 p.m. with maintenance-schedule precision
Opens the private redesign folder at 2 a.m. most nights
Pauses before using someone's name, as if confirming the right file
breaking_points: The Shelf filtration node reaching catastrophic failure on her watch
The disappeared whistleblower resurfacing with the original documents
Her private folder being accessed by someone inside the Spire
Nadira obtaining infrastructure documents with Mireille's signature
